data.description:
## Problem (PROVEN, not inferred)

`apply_inbound_records.py` derives the inbound identity provider AND creation channel from the
configured backend's vendor string:

    vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor          # 'jira-datacenter' for DC
    rebar.ensure_identity_for(vendor, account_id, ..., creation_channel=vendor)

But the store vocabulary does not contain that value:

    CREATION_CHANNELS = frozenset({'cli', 'mcp', 'python', 'jira', 'import', 'unknown'})

Measured directly against a scratch repo:

    creation_channel='jira'            ext=acct-cloud -> returned '4802-2404-6de4-4167'
    creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> RAISED ValueError:
        invalid creation_channel 'jira-datacenter'; must be one of
        ['cli', 'import', 'jira', 'mcp', 'python']

(The failure only appears on a FRESH mint — an existing (provider, external_id) mapping is reused
idempotently and never reaches validation, which is why a naive probe shows a false pass.)

## Why it is SILENT — the part that makes this dangerous

The call is wrapped in:

    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply
        logger.debug('inbound: could not ensure identity for jira accountId %r', ...)

So on a Data Center deployment EVERY inbound ghost-identity mint fails, is swallowed, and is
reported only at DEBUG. The reconcile pass still converges and reports success. This is precisely
the failure mode epic e369's AC6 exists to catch: a swallowed exception can still converge, so
convergence is not evidence of correctness.

Consequence: DC inbound assignees never get identities minted, so assignee resolution degrades
silently on every DC pass.

## Why it is newly reachable

Before story J7 [rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1], `reconciler.backend` was validated as
`_as_choice(v, k, {'jira'})`, so config could NEVER select the DC backend and
`select_backend(load_config()).vendor` could never return 'jira-datacenter'. J7 widens that
choice set — which is what ACTIVATES this path. The defect is latent on main today and becomes
live the moment a DC deployment is configured.

## Also inconsistent WITHIN the same module

The ticket-creation path a few lines below already hard-codes the family channel:

    create_data['creation_channel'] = validate_creation_channel('jira')

So the ticket gets 'jira' while the identity path tries 'jira-datacenter'. One of the two is wrong;
per epic e369's shared-identity decision (DC-created tickets carry the SHARED 'jira' creation
channel and the deployment is distinguished by RemoteRef.instance, so nothing in the store
vocabulary forks per deployment), the ticket path is right and the identity path is the bug.

## Proposed fix (NOT to widen the vocabulary)

Map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel at this call site, so both jira and jira-datacenter
mint under the shared 'jira' provider/channel. Adding 'jira-datacenter' to CREATION_CHANNELS is
the WRONG fix: it forks the store vocabulary per deployment, contradicting the epic's decision and
dragging in a migration + compatibility gate that the epic explicitly avoids. It would also
fragment identity across deployments (a Cloud and a DC identity for the same human).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity successfully, asserted by a test
      that FAILS on today's code
- [ ] the identity is minted under the shared 'jira' provider/channel, matching the ticket path
- [ ] a test asserts the failure is not merely swallowed — i.e. the mint is observed to SUCCEED,
      not that no exception escaped
- [ ] CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED (no per-deployment vocabulary fork, no migration)
data.title: DC inbound identity mint fails silently: 'jira-datacenter' is not a valid creation_channel
